subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should valid ignore files below the 4 MiB read limit be terminally excluded when they exceed the new pattern-complexity budgets?
rationale: This is an upgrade-visible workspace-discovery policy change, not a mechanical correction to the unbounded file-read bug, and current-main behavior did not impose the new terminal-deny budgets.

options.title: Preserve valid under-cap behavior
options.body: Retain the bounded file read but remove or redesign terminal complexity denial so valid files below the published byte limit continue to apply their ignore rules.

options.title: Adopt terminal complexity denial
options.body: Keep the rule budgets as an intentional security and availability policy, document the changed discovery behavior, and add exact-head proof for both normal and denied policies.

recommendation.title: Preserve valid under-cap behavior
recommendation.body: Retain the bounded file read but remove or redesign terminal complexity denial so valid files below the published byte limit continue to apply their ignore rules.

likelyOwner.reason: Steipete is assigned to this PR and authored the recent scan-hardening commits that introduced the reviewed policy surface.
